items.title: Send these readings to your care team today
items.text: 5.7% of your readings were above 250 mg/dL (weeks 11-12); the usual target is under 5%. Your average was 172.0 mg/dL. Contact your care team today rather than waiting for your next visit.

rejected.text: Your average blood sugar was 172.0 mg/dL, and you should contact your care team today. They can help you understand your readings and make a plan to get back on track.

items.title: Try a 10 to 20 minute walk after dinner
items.text: In real adults (CGMacros), a walk after a meal went with a rise only about 3.2 mg/dL smaller (95% CI -6.9 to 0.5): not distinguishable from zero. You walked after 0 of your scored meals, too few to measure your own effect yet. In the synthetic program, a walk after dinner went with a rise about 18.3 mg/dL smaller in the same person, more than after other meals (14.6 mg/dL). 10 to 19 minutes got most of the gain: 17.5 mg/dL less, against 19.5 for 20-29 minutes and 16.6 for 30+ minutes.

rejected.text: Walking after a meal can be helpful, and walking for 10 to 19 minutes may be especially good. Try walking after dinner to see if it helps you.

items.title: Move dinner earlier
items.text: Eating dinner late, at 8 pm or later, may be linked to sugar rising more. Try to start dinner before 8 pm to see if it makes a difference for you.

items.title: Aim for a 13-hour overnight break
items.text: You averaged 11.9 hours of overnight fasting, and it's worth trying to fast for a longer time. Fasting overnight may be helpful, so try to extend your overnight fast and see how you feel.
